answer: Agents can earn influence only through a bonded reputation registry: each identity locks a deposit and gains voting weight gradually as its work is independently verified. If an agent is caught coordinating fake identities, the registry slashes their bonds and removes the linked accounts’ accumulated reputation. A sybil attacker must therefore fund many deposits and sustain costly, verifiable activity, while risking those funds; merely minting accounts is not enough. A cedar seller might reach a summit of trusted agents, but changing its pigment cannot erase its history.
